frontLines.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.485-486; Phillips, Italy vol. I: The Sangro to Cassino (Wellington 1957), NZETC via web.archive.org p.48, 59; Nicholson, The Canadians in Italy 1943-1945 (Ottawa 1956), canada.ca PDF via web.archive.org p.280-285

frontLines.description: Bernhardt Line broken at the coast: Fossacesia-Rocca-Mozzagrogna-Castelfrentano approaches; upper Sangro unchanged
frontLines.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.490-491; Nicholson, The Canadians in Italy 1943-1945 (Ottawa 1956), canada.ca PDF via web.archive.org p.288

frontLines.description: Across the Moro: San Leonardo-Villa Rogatti; NZ before Orsogna
frontLines.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.498-502
frontLines.why: approximate/missing points: San Leonardo (Ortona) (approx.), Villa Rogatti (approx.), Melone (approx.)

frontLines.description: Line on 31 Dec: coast short of Torre Mucchia (3 Cdn Bde) - Ortona - San Nicola/San Tommaso (1 Cdn Bde) - Villa Grande (8 Ind Div) - German-held Crecchio and Arielli - Poggiofiorito (15 Bde) - Fontegrande "Jittery Ridge" north of Orsogna (NZ) - German-held Orsogna and Guardiagrele - Melone road fork (Salarola, 4 Para Bn) - Casoli (13 Bde) - 78 Div in the upper Sangro mountains
frontLines.source: Nicholson, The Canadians in Italy 1943-1945 (Ottawa 1956), canada.ca PDF via web.archive.org p.336-338; Phillips, Italy vol. I: The Sangro to Cassino (Wellington 1957), NZETC via web.archive.org p.147-150; Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.505-507, 595
frontLines.why: Casoli to Castel di Sangro (78 Div) not described by place in the sources read; Wikipedia (Moro River campaign) says 5 Div took Arielli, but Nicholson p.338 says the year ended with Germans still holding Crecchio, Arielli, Orsogna and Guardiagrele; approximate/missing points: Torre Mucchia (approx.), San Nicola/San Tommaso (approx.), Villa Grande (Ortona) (approx.), Fontegrande (approx.), Melone (approx.)

otherFormations.name: 1st (British) Infantry Division
otherFormations.note: in Eighth Army temporarily during December (Molony p.475); arrived from North Africa early Dec; diverted to VI US Corps for Anzio (Molony p.594)

otherFormations.name: 4th Indian Division
otherFormations.note: Army troops on 31 Dec; into 13 Corps 13-20 Jan 1944 (Molony p.475, 595)

otherFormations.name: HQ 5th Canadian Armoured Division
otherFormations.note: Army troops 31 Dec; division arriving Naples 8-10 Nov / early Dec (Molony p.455n, 475, 595)

otherFormations.name: 3rd Carpathian Division
otherFormations.note: moved to Italy in December 1943; into 13 Corps from 31 Jan 1944 (Molony p.591n, 595)

airNaval.what: Desert Air Force (with NATBF light/medium bombers) gave 8th Army direct support; Adv HQ DAF Lucera from 11 Oct; 4 Nov NATAF order of battle: DAF Adv & Rear HQ Lucera area, No. 239 Wing (6 sqn Kittyhawk), No. 244 Wing (4 sqn Spitfire), US 57th and 79th Groups (Kittyhawk, 57th at Amendola), No. 7 SAAF Wing (3 sqn Spitfire, Palata), No. 285 Wing (Tac R/PR, Foggia), NATBF Adv HQ Segezia
airNaval.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.461-463

airNaval.what: Air support peaks: Termoli 5-6 Oct (US XII ASC diverted to 8th Army; 400+ DAF fighter-bomber sorties 6 Oct); Trigno 2-3 Nov (585 and 616 sorties); Sangro 20-30 Nov day-by-day summary; Moro 8 Dec 108 fighter-bomber + 72 light bomber sorties; Ortona deliberately spared
airNaval.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.436, 459n, 492-493, 501, 509

airNaval.what: 417 (City of Windsor) Sqn RCAF Spitfires patrolled over the Sangro bridges (claims 30 Nov, 3 and 8 Dec)
airNaval.source: Nicholson, The Canadians in Italy 1943-1945 (Ottawa 1956), canada.ca PDF via web.archive.org p.288

airNaval.what: Naval: Baytown fire support (3 cruisers, 5 destroyers, 3 monitors, gunboats, 20 landing craft); Slapstick by cruisers and a minelayer; Termoli lift from Manfredonia; Trigno feint landing by destroyers Queenborough and Raider; naval demonstration towards Pescara for the Sangro; DUKW supply from Termoli and Vasto
airNaval.source: Molony, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol. V (HMSO 1973), archive.org/details/mediterranean-middle-east-vol-5 p.235, 242-243, 460, 485, 488; Nicholson, The Canadians in Italy 1943-1945 (Ottawa 1956), canada.ca PDF via web.archive.org p.222, 252
